results.title: Problem profiles: Factory farming
results.content: * Even if nonhuman animals don’t morally matter as much as humans, there’s good evidence that they are conscious and that they feel pain — and, as a result, the poor conditions in factory farms are likely causing animals to experience severe suffering. This is also just a rough proxy for the scale of the issue; before slaughter, these animals are almost always kept in factory farming conditions, where we’d guess they suffer great harms. If we include *invertebrates* (e.g. octopuses, insects, crabs, snails, shrimp) — which is more controversial because we have less evidence of their ability to feel pain — it’s more like 1.6–4.5 trillion farmed animals killed per year, and around 350–700 billion animals alive in farms at any given time.3 It’s much harder to estimate how many of these animals are in *factory* farms. We’re a bit more optimistic than that, as we’d guess that if there were clear alternative products, it would be much easier to both push for increased welfare on farms and to convince people to stop eating factory-farmed meat.↩
